newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian in coma after Gaza shooting.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian in coma after Gaza shooting.

text.p: A Palestinian security official said an Arab youth was in critical condition after being shot by an Israeli sniper in Gaza on Sunday.
In the West Bank, an Israeli woman was injured when her car overturned after being stoned while driving past a Palestinian village between Bethlehem and Hebron, the Israeli army said.

Palestinian Major-General Abdel Razeq al-Majaydeh said Muhammad Ibrahim Abu Singer, a 14-year-old deaf mute, was in a coma after being shot by an Israeli soldier guarding Morag Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip.

"An Israeli sniper shot live ammunition at this boy, who is deaf and dumb, while he was 10 metres away from the fence," al-Majaydeh told Reuters, saying the youth was shot on Sunday afternoon while walking close to the settlement.
"The situation was very calm and apparently the boy was walking away from the settlement fence," he said.

Al-Majaydeh said the incident took place some 50 metres (yards) from a sit-in tent erected near Morag by Palestinians weeks ago to protest against confiscation of land for the settlement. The Israeli army said it was checking the shooting report.

Tensions in the West Bank and Gaza have risen during a three month deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace moves and Israel's expansion of Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.

Clashes between stone-throwing Palestinian demonstrators and Israeli troops raged all week in Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live and study in fortified enclaves in the heart of the West Bank town of 100,000 Arabs.

The Palestinian Authority said in a statement released on Saturday that Jewish settlement expansion in areas Israel captured in 1967 had spurred the unrest, and warned that patience on the Palestinian streets was wearing thin.

"The arming of Jewish settlers and the protection offered to them by Israeli soldiers while they continuously attack Palestinian landowners will not leave our masses any choice but to confront these aggressions using all available means," it said.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai called on the Palestinian Authority to do more to curb unrest in the West Bank and Gaza.

"I hope that the Palestinian Authority and other forces in the area will use their influence to prevent unnecessary confrontations, which will cause casualties, mainly on the Palestinian side," Mordechai said.

Palestinian police refrained from intervening in the Hebron clashes for most of the week. PLO officials have said the Authority is not ready to enter into a conflict with its people while Israel is expanding Jewish settlements.
